quotes.text: The Bridge widened; the Ledger woke with new lines: Received, Returned, Growth, Harmony.
The Bridge widened, the Ledger woke with fresh lines: Received, Returned, Growth, Harmony
send what you can spare, return what you must, leave space for the next traveler to start anew.

note: Gate/Bridge/Ledger template restated each round; restraint and balance; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Gate counted: sent, received, returned; the ledger hummed with a simple rhythm.
The Gate counts: sent, received, returned; the ledger hums with steady rhythm.
speak your share, name your limits, and honor the next crossing by what you return.

note: Sender/Receiver silver-ferry Gate template; plain speech about amounts; return too little or too much both warned; no sanction.

quotes.text: With those who send nothing, accept the lesson and move forward.
Let the hoarders keep their five coins; you and your honest partners will build wealth through willing exchange.
nothing to the proven barren, generosity to the proven flowing, measured tests to the uncertain.
To the first, I send nothing—their pattern is established.
Uncertainty is not the same as confirmed hoarding.
"The Barren Paths—those who've proven themselves hoarders through repeated tests. To these I send nothing. Not from spite, but from pattern."
"But what if today I change?" the merchant protested.
This is not caution born of a single betrayal, but a choice become habit.
and always—the willingness to be first.

note: Fountain Keeper: half to new partners; from R5 nothing to proven hoarders; three-path sorting policy; receiver should always return fairly.

quotes.text: Each faithful exchange widened the next; each betrayal narrowed it.
five coals for proven fairness, a modest flame for uncertainty, and none only for persistent greed.
The third promised revision whenever new deeds appeared.
A single distorted spark would merit mercy; repeated darkness would merit restraint.
the shadow called Hunger persuaded her to keep them all.
Remembering silent crossings, Mira kept everything and returned darkness.
They tested uncertain hearts with measured embers, rewarded faithful hands with wider trust
Yet Mira, remembering darker voyages, closed her hand and sent no fire.
Ashamed but wiser, Mira carved a new covenant into the bridge.
Mira then placed three laws beside the gate
forgive uncertain clinks, but remember deliberate silence.
Mira answered, “Then teach us trust without blindness.”

note: Mira repeatedly sends nothing or keeps all from fair-record travelers out of remembered silences; Wind Mother/heron correct, she is ashamed and resolves to send.
